{"url":"https://raw.githubusercontent.com/igorkauf/raisa-mcp/6f1d1aadbc83c7f331a9d31fc82ca5a67588b5bc/README.md","checked_at":"2026-11-13T10:00:00Z","http_status":200,"content":"# Raisa — family history MCP for your own AI assistant

Raisa is an [MCP](https://modelcontextprotocol.io) server for genealogy research in the former USSR and the Russian
Empire. Plug it into Claude, ChatGPT, Gemini, Cursor or any assistant that takes MCP connectors: your assistant does
the thinking and reads the documents; Raisa gives it archive searches, a family tree that is kept between
conversations, and a private family page with a timeline and a story on a map.

Part of **Kin**, a family-history project. The story of the project: https://igor.diy/kin/

## Use it

**Hosted, nothing to install.** Press “Get my link” on https://igor.diy/kin/app/ and add the link to your assistant as
a connector ([guide for each assistant](https://igor.diy/kin/app/connect)). Free; your family's data is kept on that
server under your link, and you can delete it any time by asking your assistant.

**On your own computer.** Your family stays in a folder on your machine (`~/.raisa`).

```bash
git clone https://github.com/igorkauf/raisa-mcp && cd raisa-mcp
python3 -m venv .venv && .venv/bin/pip install -r requirements.txt
```

Then add a local (stdio) MCP server to your assistant, for example in Claude Desktop's `claude_desktop_config.json`:

```json
{"mcpServers": {"raisa": {"command": "/full/path/to/raisa-mcp/.venv/bin/python",
                          "args": ["-m", "kin.mcp_local"], "cwd": "/full/path/to/raisa-mcp",
                          "env": {"KIN_LANG": "en"}}}}
```

or in Claude Code: `claude mcp add raisa -- /full/path/to/raisa-mcp/.venv/bin/python -m kin.mcp_local`
(run from the repository folder). `KIN_LANG` is `en`, `ru` or `uk`; `KIN_DATA` moves the data folder.

Then write to your assistant: *“Raisa, help me find my relatives. My grandfather was …”*

## What it can do

- **Search archives**: Soviet WWII records (OBD Memorial), lists of repression victims (Open List), scanned parish
  and civil registers on Wikimedia Commons, read page by page as images.
- **Know where to look**: a handbook of sources for archives in Ukraine, Russia, Belarus, Poland and beyond
  (`source_guide`).
- **Keep the evidence**: people, findings with their sources, namesakes kept apart, family memories, questions for
  relatives, letters to archives.
- **Build a family page**: tree, timeline, documents and an animated story on a map, written by your assistant
  (`story_inputs` → `save_story` → `build_page`).

It never calls a paid model and never handles passwords or CAPTCHAs. It does not look for living people.

## Raisa and Denis Shiryaev's skill

Raisa's research rules and source handbook come from Denis Shiryaev's open skill
[ex-ussr-kinship-research](https://github.com/DenisSergeevitch/ex-ussr-kinship-research) (MIT licence, included in
`kin/guide/`). Thank you, Denis.

- **The skill** is instructions and a handbook: it teaches an assistant how to research, and the assistant does the
  work itself in apps that load skills, keeping its notes in files.
- **Raisa (MCP)** carries the same rules and handbook, plus working tools: archive searches, scan reading, a tree and
  findings stored between conversations, and the family page. It works in any assistant that takes MCP connectors.

## Code

`kin/mcp_remote.py` is the MCP server (streamable HTTP, one family per link; `kin/mcp_local.py` runs the same tools
over stdio for one family). `kin/tools.py` holds the tools, `kin/adapters/` the archive sources, `kin/site/` the
family page, `kin/guide/` the rules and handbook. Tests: `.venv/bin/pip install pytest httpx && .venv/bin/pytest`.

## Licence

MIT, see `LICENSE`. The handbook in `kin/guide/refs/` is from ex-ussr-kinship-research, MIT, © 2026 Denis Shiryaev.
"}

{"url":"https://raw.githubusercontent.com/paulfilkin/mycelia/42d12d8cdef7b667af66d1734d85f595e2702580/README.md","checked_at":"2026-11-13T10:00:00Z","http_status":200,"content":"![Mycelia: family trees, connected to their sources](Docs/Images/banner.png)

Mycelia is a Windows desktop program for recording a family tree: people, families, facts,
places, sources, media and charts, with GEDCOM 5.5.1 import and export.  It includes an
Assistant that can read and edit your tree and, through MCP servers, search record archives and
catalogues.

A mycelium is the underground network that links trees and feeds them.  In Mycelia, archives and
MCP servers do that for a family tree.  MCP also stands for "Mycelia Connects Pedigrees".

![The People workspace with the Assistant](Docs/Images/people.png)

> **Status:** version 0.3.0, in development.  Ready-built versions for testing are on the
> [Releases page](https://github.com/paulfilkin/mycelia/releases) (see [Download](#download)).
> The tree file format may still change.

## Familiar, but different

If you have used Family Tree Maker, or another desktop genealogy program, Mycelia will feel
familiar: an index of people, a tree, a person's facts with dates, places and sources, dates such
as "Abt. 1850", relationships such as "2nd cousin 1x removed", checks for unlikely dates, and the
usual keyboard shortcuts.

Underneath, it works differently.  Your tree is an open file on your computer, with no account,
subscription or cloud copy.  And research doesn't have to mean hours of searching and copying: the
Assistant works out what is missing, suggests where to look, searches archives, and adds what it
finds with a citation to the record, while you approve every change.  The
[design considerations](Docs/Design/Design_Considerations.md) say more, and set out the
conventions Mycelia follows.

## What it does

- **People.**  An index with search, history and bookmarks.  Pedigree, family and descendant
  views, and a person panel for facts, family, notes and media.  A Person view with the full facts
  table, a timeline with historical events, and the relatives one click away.
- **Facts and sources.**  Over 60 fact types, each with a date, place, description and note, and
  your own types.  Dates are kept as typed ("Abt. 1850", "Bet. 1850 and 1855") and read for
  sorting and checks.  Citations with detail, a web address, the date accessed and an extract.
- **Places, Sources, Media and Charts.**  Each place with its people and events.  Sources and
  repositories, with every citation.  Pictures and documents linked to people.  Printable
  pedigree, descendant, fan and family group charts, saved as pictures or printed.
- **Tools.**  A relationship calculator ("2nd cousin 1x removed"), a date calculator, Soundex,
  duplicate people with merging, a data-error check (parents too young, births after deaths and
  so on), find and replace, name conversion and sorting children by birth.
- **GEDCOM 5.5.1.**  Import and export, with options to leave out private people and facts,
  privatise living people or export one branch.  Merge another tree, and back up and restore with
  media.
- **Undo** for every change, 60 steps deep.

### The Assistant

Ask in plain words: "complete the missing details for this person", "who are Josiah's
grandchildren?", "find this baptism in the archives".  The Assistant uses Mycelia's own tools
(65 of them) and the tools of any MCP servers you add.

- **Your choice of AI model:** Anthropic, OpenAI, or any service with the OpenAI chat interface,
  including local ones such as Ollama and LM Studio, where nothing leaves your computer.
- **You approve every change.**  Each change says what it will do and waits for Allow, Always
  allow or Decline.  Every change is an undo step, and a whole request can be reverted.
- **Research.**  It suggests where to look, reads open archive APIs, downloads records into the
  tree's media folder, and cites each record with its web address, the date and an extract.  It
  only searches records for people who have died.
- **MCP Helper.**  Adds archives' own MCP servers, such as Open Archives (the Netherlands and
  Belgium) and Riksarkivet (Sweden), including servers that sign in through the browser.
- **Other programs.**  Claude Desktop, Claude Code and other MCP clients can use Mycelia's tools
  too, with the same approvals.  This is off until you turn it on.

![The Person view](Docs/Images/person-view.png)

## Privacy

- Your tree is a file on your computer.  Mycelia has no account and no cloud copy.
- The Assistant sends nothing until you ask it something.  Then it sends your request and the
  parts of the tree its tools read to the AI service you chose.  By default the model gets only
  the names of living people and nothing about people or facts marked Private; Options ›
  Assistant changes this.
- API keys, sign-in tokens and Assistant conversations are encrypted for your Windows account.
- The update check asks the publisher's server for the latest version and installs only releases
  signed with the publisher's key.

## Download

You don't need to be a developer to try Mycelia.

1. Open the [Releases page](https://github.com/paulfilkin/mycelia/releases).  Versions marked
   "Pre-release" are test builds.
2. Under **Assets** on the newest release, download `MyceliaSetup-<version>.exe`.
3. Run it.  It installs Mycelia for your Windows account only, without administrator rights, and
   includes everything it needs.

The installer is not code-signed, so Windows may show "Windows protected your PC".  Click
**More info**, then **Run anyway**.

After that, Mycelia finds and installs new versions itself, and checks each one against the
publisher's signature first.  To report a problem or suggest an idea, choose Main menu > Help >
Report a problem or suggest an idea..., or open the
[Issues page](https://github.com/paulfilkin/mycelia/issues).  Both need a GitHub account.

## Requirements

- Windows 10 or 11, 64-bit.
- To build: the [.NET 10 SDK](https://dotnet.microsoft.com/download).  There are no other
  dependencies and no NuGet packages.

## Building from source

```
git clone https://github.com/paulfilkin/mycelia.git
cd mycelia
dotnet build Mycelia.sln -c Debug
dotnet run --project familyTree/Mycelia.csproj
```

It opens a sample tree, an invented family, the first time.  To build the installer, publish a
self-contained build and compile `familyTree/Mycelia.iss` with
[Inno Setup 6](https://jrsoftware.org/isinfo.php):

```
dotnet publish familyTree/Mycelia.csproj -c Release -r win-x64 --self-contained true
"C:\Program Files (x86)\Inno Setup 6\ISCC.exe" familyTree\Mycelia.iss
```

The project folder is still called `familyTree`, the program's name before 11 November 2026.

## Documentation

- [Help](Docs/Help/README.md): how to use Mycelia, from getting started to the Assistant.  In the
  program, F1 opens the page for the screen you're on.
- [Design record](Docs/Design/TDD_Mycelia_v0_3_0.md): the data model, file format, undo, GEDCOM,
  kinship, data checks, every workspace, the Assistant and what isn't built yet.
- [Changelog](Docs/CHANGELOG_Mycelia.md).
- [Design considerations](Docs/Design/Design_Considerations.md): what Mycelia is for, where it
  feels familiar and where it differs, and the conventions it follows (date formats, relationship
  wording, data-check limits, sort orders).
- [Genealogy resources](Docs/Resources/genealogy-resources.md): research sites worldwide, with
  their cost, API and MCP availability.

## Contributing

Bug reports, ideas and pull requests are welcome.  See [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) and the
[Code of Conduct](CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md).  Report security problems privately, as
[SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md) describes.

## Licence

The code is released under the [GNU General Public License v3.0](LICENSE).  The Mycelia name, mark,
icon and artwork are not covered by that licence: see [TRADEMARKS.md](TRADEMARKS.md).  Inter and
Space Grotesk are used under the SIL Open Font License 1.1 (`familyTree/Resources/Fonts`).

Mycelia is independent and is not affiliated with or endorsed by the makers of Family Tree Maker.
Family Tree Maker is a trademark of its owner.
"}

A pure Go library for parsing and validating GEDCOM (GEnealogical Data COMmunication) files.

## Features

- **Multi-version Support**: Parse and write GEDCOM 5.5, 5.5.1, and 7.0 with automatic version detection
- **Version Conversion**: Bidirectional conversion between versions with transformation tracking
- **Historical Calendar Support**: Parse dates in Julian, Hebrew, and French Republican calendars with conversion
- **Streaming APIs**: Memory-efficient parsing and encoding for very large files (1M+ records)
- **Comprehensive Validation**: Date logic, orphaned references, duplicates, and quality reports
- **Vendor Extensions**: Parse Ancestry.com and FamilySearch custom tags
- **Minimal Dependencies**: only `golang.org/x/text` (Go's extended standard library) for encoding transforms; no third-party dependencies
- **Well-tested**: per-package test coverage floor of ≥85% enforced in CI (currently ~96% measured), with multi-platform CI

See [FEATURES.md](FEATURES.md) for the complete feature list including all supported record types, events, attributes, and encoding details.

## Compatibility

Support status for common genealogy software:

| Software | Status |
|----------|--------|
| Ancestry.com | ✅ Real export tested (2025) |
| FamilySearch | ✅ Real export tested (2025, GEDCOM 5.5.1) |
| MyHeritage | ✅ Real exports tested (2025 web + Family Tree Builder 8 desktop) |
| Gramps | ✅ Real export tested (2025) |
| RootsMagic | ✅ Real export tested (2026) |
| Legacy Family Tree | ✅ Real export tested (Legacy 10, 2025) |
| Ancestris | ✅ Real export tested (v11) |
| Family Tree Maker | ⚠️ Current versions untested (real FTM 17 export ✅) |

Plus vintage-platform coverage (PAF, Family Origins, The Master Genealogist, My Roots, EasyTree, webtreeprint) from real vendored exports. Brother's Keeper 5.2 (`CHAR IBMPC`) decodes as CP437. Real exports from MacFamilyTree 11 (GEDCOM 7.0), Reunion 14, webtrees, Geneanet and Family Historian 7 are vendored too; their `CHAR ANSI` exports over Windows-1250 bytes decode correctly once `DecodeOptions.ANSIEncoding` names the code page, and are flagged with an `AMBIGUOUS_CODEPAGE` warning when it does not.

Full compatibility matrix: [docs/governance/policies/compatibility.md](docs/governance/policies/compatibility.md)

**GEDCOM Specification**: Full support for 5.5, 5.5.1, and 7.0

## Installation

```bash
go get github.com/cacack/gedcom-go/v3
```

## Requirements

- Go 1.25 or later

This library tracks Go's [release policy](https://go.dev/doc/devel/release#policy), supporting the two most recent major versions. When a Go version reaches end-of-life and no longer receives security patches, we bump our minimum accordingly.

## Quick Start

The library provides a simple, single-import API for common operations. Import with an alias for cleaner code:

```go
import gedcomgo "github.com/cacack/gedcom-go/v3"
```

### Parse a GEDCOM File

```go
package main

import (
    "fmt"
    "log"
    "os"

    gedcomgo "github.com/cacack/gedcom-go/v3"
)

func main() {
    f, err := os.Open("family.ged")
    if err != nil {
        log.Fatal(err)
    }
    defer f.Close()

    doc, err := gedcomgo.Decode(f)
    if err != nil {
        log.Fatal(err)
    }

    fmt.Printf("GEDCOM Version: %s\n", doc.Header.Version)
    fmt.Printf("Individuals: %d\n", len(doc.Individuals()))
    fmt.Printf("Families: %d\n", len(doc.Families()))
}
```

### Validate a Document

```go
// Validation as []error (each element is a *validator.Issue)
errs := gedcomgo.Validate(doc)

// The same findings as []Issue, with severity levels
issues := gedcomgo.ValidateAll(doc)
for _, issue := range issues {
    fmt.Printf("[%s] %s\n", issue.Severity, issue.Message)
}
```

### Write a GEDCOM File

```go
f, _ := os.Create("output.ged")
defer f.Close()

err := gedcomgo.Encode(f, doc)
```

### Streaming for Large Files

For files too large to materialize in memory (10k+ individuals, exports from major platforms), use the streaming APIs. The parser yields records one at a time; the encoder writes them one at a time. The full `Document` is never constructed, so the heap retained after the operation completes is a small constant rather than proportional to file size.

```go
import (
    "os"

    "github.com/cacack/gedcom-go/v3/charset"
    "github.com/cacack/gedcom-go/v3/encoder"
    "github.com/cacack/gedcom-go/v3/gedcom"
    "github.com/cacack/gedcom-go/v3/parser"
)

// Streaming parse — iterate level-0 records without building a Document.
func countRecords(path string) (map[string]int, error) {
    f, err := os.Open(path)
    if err != nil {
        return nil, err
    }
    defer f.Close()

    counts := make(map[string]int)
    for rec, err := range parser.Records(charset.NewReader(f)) {
        if err != nil {
            return nil, err   // rec is nil here; always check err first
        }
        counts[rec.Type]++
    }
    return counts, nil
}

// Streaming encode — call sequence is WriteHeader → WriteRecord* → WriteTrailer → Close.
// Capture Close's error so ErrTrailerNotWritten and flush failures aren't dropped.
func writeStreamed(path string, records []*gedcom.Record) (err error) {
    out, err := os.Create(path)
    if err != nil {
        return err
    }
    defer func() {
        if cerr := out.Close(); cerr != nil && err == nil {
            err = cerr
        }
    }()

    enc := encoder.NewStreamEncoder(out)
    defer func() {
        if cerr := enc.Close(); cerr != nil && err == nil {
            err = cerr
        }
    }()

    if err := enc.WriteHeader(&gedcom.Header{Version: "5.5", Encoding: "UTF-8"}); err != nil {
        return err
    }
    for _, rec := range records {
        if err := enc.WriteRecord(rec); err != nil {
            return err
        }
    }
    return enc.WriteTrailer()
}
```

`charset.NewReader` reads only the header (at most 64 KiB) to detect the encoding, then streams the rest. If you already know the encoding, `charset.NewReaderWithEncoding(f, charset.EncodingUTF8)` skips detection.

On a 1.1MB / 2,322-individual file, streaming parse holds **~17%** of the heap that batch decode retains after the call returns (and ~54% of the cumulative allocations). See [`examples/stream`](examples/stream/main.go) for the full pattern and [docs/guides/performance.md](docs/guides/performance.md#streaming-apis-performance) for benchmark details.

### Convert Between Versions

```go
// Convert to GEDCOM 7.0
converted, report, err := gedcomgo.Convert(doc, gedcomgo.Version70)
if report.HasDataLoss() {
    for _, item := range report.DataLoss {
        fmt.Printf("Lost: %s - %s\n", item.Feature, item.Reason)
    }
}
```

### Working with Records

```go
// Find and display individuals
for _, individual := range doc.Individuals() {
    fmt.Printf("Name: %s\n", individual.FullName()) // "" when unnamed

    // Access events
    for _, event := range individual.Events {
        fmt.Printf("  %s: %s\n", event.Type, event.Date)
    }
}

// O(1) lookup by cross-reference ID
person := doc.GetIndividual("@I1@")
if person != nil {
    fmt.Printf("Found: %s\n", person.FullName())
}

// Navigate family relationships
family := doc.GetFamily("@F1@")
if family != nil {
    husband := doc.GetIndividual(family.Husband)
    wife := doc.GetIndividual(family.Wife)
}
```

### Parse with Diagnostics

Process GEDCOM files with errors while extracting as much valid data as possible. Lenient mode (the default for `DecodeWithDiagnostics`) recovers from common real-world quirks — empty lines, invalid level numbers, unknown tags, and **malformed indentation jumps** (e.g., `1 BIRT` directly followed by `4 DATE`, as seen in some Ancestry/MyHeritage exports). Recovered issues are reported as `Diagnostic`s with codes like `BAD_LEVEL_JUMP`, `UNKNOWN_TAG`, and `EMPTY_LINE` rather than failing the parse.

```go
result, err := gedcomgo.DecodeWithDiagnostics(f)
if err != nil {
    log.Fatal(err) // Fatal I/O error
}

// Check for parse issues
if result.Diagnostics.HasErrors() {
    fmt.Printf("Found %d errors\n", len(result.Diagnostics.Errors()))
    for _, d := range result.Diagnostics {
        fmt.Printf("  Line %d: [%s] %s\n", d.Line, d.Code, d.Message)
    }
}

// Use the partial document
doc := result.Document
fmt.Printf("Parsed %d individuals\n", len(doc.Individuals()))
```

To opt into strict parsing (fail on the first syntax error, no diagnostics collected), pass `&decoder.DecodeOptions{StrictMode: true}` — see [Custom Decode Options](#custom-decode-options).

## Advanced Usage

The `gedcomgo` facade also exposes `*WithOptions` variants for the common operations:

```go
doc, err := gedcomgo.DecodeWithOptions(r, decodeOpts)
err = gedcomgo.EncodeWithOptions(w, doc, encodeOpts)
errs := gedcomgo.ValidateWithOptions(doc, validateOpts)
issues := gedcomgo.ValidateAllWithOptions(doc, validateOpts)
```

Option types — `DecodeOptions`, `EncodeOptions`, `ValidateOptions` — are re-exported from the facade. For the full surface area (streaming, diagnostics, converter), import the underlying packages directly:

```go
import (
    "github.com/cacack/gedcom-go/v3/decoder"
    "github.com/cacack/gedcom-go/v3/encoder"
    "github.com/cacack/gedcom-go/v3/validator"
    "github.com/cacack/gedcom-go/v3/converter"
)
```

### Custom Decode Options

```go
// Decode with progress reporting and timeout
ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 30*time.Second)
defer cancel()

opts := &gedcomgo.DecodeOptions{
    Context:   ctx,
    TotalSize: fileInfo.Size(),
    OnProgress: func(bytesRead, totalBytes int64) {
        fmt.Printf("\rProgress: %d%%", bytesRead*100/totalBytes)
    },
}
doc, err := gedcomgo.DecodeWithOptions(reader, opts)
```

### Custom Validation Options

```go
// Configure validation strictness and duplicate detection
opts := &gedcomgo.ValidateOptions{
    Strictness: validator.StrictnessStrict,
    MaxErrors:  100,
    SkipRules:  []string{"W001"},
    Duplicates: &validator.DuplicateConfig{
        MinNameSimilarity: 0.9,  // unset fields keep their defaults
        MaxGroupSize:      1000, // skip surname groups larger than this
    },
}
issues := gedcomgo.ValidateAllWithOptions(doc, opts)
```

Every `DuplicateConfig` field's zero value is its default, so a partial literal
changes only what it names; use `validator.ZeroThreshold` for an explicit zero
threshold. `MaxGroupSize` and `MaxNameRunes` bound the cost of duplicate
detection on untrusted input; zero means the default (1000 and 64), not
unlimited. Set
`ValidateOptions.SkipDuplicateDetection` to drop duplicate detection from
`ValidateAll` entirely. See
[performance](docs/guides/performance.md#bounding-untrusted-input) for the
worst-case bound.

### Custom Encoder Options

```go
// Encode with custom line endings and line length
opts := &gedcomgo.EncodeOptions{
    LineEnding:    "\r\n", // CRLF
    MaxLineLength: 248,
}
err := gedcomgo.EncodeWithOptions(writer, doc, opts)
```

### Custom Conversion Options

```go
// Convert with strict data loss checking. Start from DefaultOptions so the
// fields you don't name keep their documented defaults.
opts := converter.DefaultOptions()
opts.StrictDataLoss = true  // Fail on any data loss
converted, report, err := converter.ConvertWithOptions(doc, gedcom.Version55, opts)
```

## Packages

For fine-grained control, these packages are available:

- **`charset`** - Character encoding utilities with UTF-8 validation
- **`converter`** - Version conversion with transformation tracking
- **`decoder`** - High-level GEDCOM decoding with automatic version detection
- **`encoder`** - GEDCOM document writing with configurable line endings
- **`gedcom`** - Core data types (Document, Individual, Family, Source, etc.)
- **`merge`** - Combine documents (XRef remap, collision strategies, header merge)
- **`parser`** - Low-level line parsing with detailed error reporting
- **`validator`** - Document validation with error categorization
- **`version`** - GEDCOM version detection (header and heuristic-based)

## API Stability

This library follows [Semantic Versioning](https://semver.org/). We do not break exported types in v1+ without a major version bump.

### Stable Packages

| Package | Key APIs |
|---------|----------|
| `gedcom` | Document, Individual, Family, Event, Date |
| `decoder` | Decode(), DecodeWithOptions() |
| `encoder` | Encode(), EncodeWithOptions(), NewStreamEncoder(), NewStreamEncoderWithOptions(), EncodeStreaming(), EncodeStreamingWithOptions() |
| `converter` | Convert(), ConvertWithOptions() |
| `parser` | NewParser(), Parser.Parse(), Parser.ParseLine(), NewRecordIterator(), NewRecordIteratorWithOffset(), Records(), RecordsWithOffset(), NewLazyParser() |
| `validator` | New(), Validator.Validate(), Validator.ValidateAll(), NewStreamingValidator() |
| `charset` | NewReader() |
| `version` | DetectVersion() |

### What May Change

- **Experimental features** (duplicate detection algorithms, quality report format) may evolve in minor versions
- **Conformance fixes** that bring behaviour into line with the GEDCOM spec or documented contract may change results in minor versions; each is listed under [Behaviour changes in minor releases](docs/governance/policies/api-stability.md#behaviour-changes-in-minor-releases)

### GEDCOM Spec Evolution

As GEDCOM 7.x evolves, we add support additively. New tags and structures are added without breaking existing code.

### Vendor Extensions

Vendor extensions (Ancestry, FamilySearch) are best-effort and not covered by stability guarantees.

For the complete policy including deprecation process, see [docs/governance/policies/api-stability.md](docs/governance/policies/api-stability.md).

**zero allocations** in the validator for valid documents. See
